steps.content: You want to see more things, but a familiar voice is already outside the door.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: You okay, old man? You lost the argument with me, and now your legs are failing, too? You agreed that the loser has to call the winner Daddy. Come on...

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Call... me... Daddy...
Accompanied by a string of curses, Doyle slams open the door, his head wrapped in bandages. Both of you are startled when you see each other.

steps.speaker: Doyle & You
steps.content: You...

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: You woke up, you little ****? Why not sleep till next year? Bug off and get some exercise. Your weak **** is dragging me down!

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: He's really worried about you.
...When did Hecate learn to interpret like this? You no longer trust her gentle messages.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: How did you get hurt so badly?

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: Oh you... Don't make a fuss. I'm perfectly fine. That bastard Gandall just wanted to make me look funny.
He tears off the bandages and tosses you a bottle. When you open it, you are overwhelmed by the familiar sweet smell. You look closely, and see Ambrosia swirling inside the opaque bottle.

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: This is what you got spiked with yesterday, right? I found it from the place, what was it called... Oh, "<color=#fb9259>Candi-bar</color>."

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: This is Ambrosia. Remember, don't let anyone else... Hey, what the ****!
The three others panic upon seeing you take a swig of Ambrosia. Doyle slams down the bottle with one hand and slaps you on the head with the other.

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: Have you lost your ******* mind? This thing will knock you out with one gulp. Who'll come wipe your *** if you start Sleepwalking again?
You smile, put the cap back on, and slip the bottle of Ambrosia into your coat pocket. You're trying to confirm one thing—just what kind of "damage" will Ambrosia cause you.

Actually, nothing. After gulping down Ambrosia, your memory is clear and your mind is coherent. You neither succumb to bewitching dreams nor vomit black goo. You just get a bit dizzy, and also a bit hungry.
Ambrosia cannot create a dream of your own, but it can share with you someone else's and drag you deep into their subconscious. How interesting, plus...

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: Plus, I know where to find the Ambrosia supplier.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: The purple-haired woman from the bar two nights ago?

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: Oh? How did you know that?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: She told me herself. I'm sure that place sells Ambrosia, and the staff there knows her. Roulecca also got her Ambrosia from her.

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: Pfft... Just odds and ends here and there.

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: Her name is <color=#fb9259>Mess</color>, and she's a self-proclaimed weaponsmith who makes and sells blades. She came to District 14 to sell Ambrosia just two weeks ago. She may not necessarily be the only supplier, but she has basically monopolized the market for affordable Ambrosia.

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: Mess keeps moving her base around, but I've pinpointed her current location. Pack up and get ready to go. Let's not let her run away.
Doyle rummages through a few drawers before finally finding a pistol and tucking it into his belt. He goes on to look for something else, but suddenly freezes, his gaze fixing on a framed photo.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Wow! What a pretty girl! Who's that guy next to her? He looks familiar. He's no hottie, but he looks pretty smart and energetic!

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Yeah, completely different from some grumpy old men we know. Why do you think that is, Doyle?
Hella really knows how to make a friend.
Doyle snatches the photo. He doesn't lose his temper. He just wipes the frame silently with his cuff, then stuffs it into the drawer half-covered. He then lowers his head and sneers at you.

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: ...I let you review the files to get to know the case. I didn't permit you to touch anything else. Mind your hands.

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: Go.
Three minutes later, Doyle opens the trunk of his beat-up car in front of you. You see a familiar face in the back seat, tied up and with a black eye.

steps.speaker: Bar Staff
steps.content: Sob... I'll tell you everything... I'll take you to Mess... Please don't hit me!

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Is this the waiter from that suspicious bar?

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: Yeah. Vital clue. Watch and learn.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: Truly an incredible inspector. A lot savvier than me.
Pffft, this is what you came up with?

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: Great minds my ***! Quit bragging.

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: Hmph. Remember, you have to take some liberties in an investigation!
You get slapped in the back of the head again.
He seems to be in a better mood. He asks the two Sinners to watch the "POW" in the backseat, and opens the driver's door himself.
Before taking the wheel, he seems to remember something. After a pause, he turns to you.

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: Oh, that reminds me. What happened last night was similar to an old case I took on a few years ago. It has been deleted from the Public Security Bureau archives. I only remember a codename—<color=#fb9259>Marv</color>.

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: This case was one of a series. The victim was addicted to a certain drink. He claimed it gave him happy dreams and helped him escape from suffering. He became more and more dependent on it... Sounds familiar?

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: The man later got sapped dry by the "happy dreams." He had a mental breakdown while sleeping, and turned into a terrifying monster. He was handed over to the FAC and became a topic I'm "not supposed to ask about."

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: It's been a few years since the incident. There's no proof that it has anything to do with this current incident, but my intuition tells me that "Sleepwalking" is by no means harmless.

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: What I'm trying to say is... A newbie like you must be extra careful handling a case like this.
You freeze for a moment, not because you are scared, but because... Doyle is worried about you.
Compared to the cases you've handled, "Marv" is nothing out of the ordinary. But since the FAC censored it, ordinary people like Doyle should not get involved.
The streets of Eastside are prosperous and peaceful. Unlike in Syndicate, the people here lead normal lives. Mania isn't a part of their lives. Nor should it be a part of Doyle's.
If possible, you don't want to ruin his life.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: You're right. Leave the rest to me.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The investigation wouldn't have gone so smoothly without you. You're an Eastsider, yet you readily accepted me and the Sinners and gave us so much help. You have my gratitude.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But what's coming up next is a battle between Sinners. None of us can predict what will happen. I cannot guarantee your safety.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: If you get infected by Mania, you will be banished from Eastside forever even if you survive. I don't want this to happen.

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: Hey newbie, I'm the inspector. It's my job to investigate. Don't think too much.

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: ...What about her? Get in the car!
He gets in the car and slams the door somewhat angrily. You sigh, send out a secret help request to the 9th Agency, and get into the front passenger seat.
The roar of the engine is accompanied by a long silence. Only after passing countless traffic lights does Doyle speak again.

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: Back when I was the "incredible inspector," I solved more cases in one month than the rest of the bureau for the whole year. I personally caught dozens of vicious scumbags and brought them to court.

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: But what I truly got out of it was not some bullshit medal, or any sense of pride or justice.

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: ...I got to see through the vile bastards behind each case. I got to see how rotten-to-the-core their souls were behind their human facades.

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content:
By comparison, your girls are model citizens. The worst they do is brag, slack off from studying, and run their mouths at me...
Haha... If I had kids, they'd probably be this rebellious, too.

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: If something goes wrong in West District, you can blame it on Mania. But there is no Mania in Eastside. All the crimes I dealt with were committed by "normal people." The only things rotten were their souls.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: The wicked are few, but you had to deal with them all.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You still uphold your duties and sense of justice even after witnessing so much evil, to the point that you're tormented by it. You are a good inspector and a respectable human being. You deserve a happy life.

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: ...Haha. See, this is why you're a newbie. You don't know **** about people.

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: What kind of a person is Doyle? A vain, emotionally out-of-control, tongue-tied, short-tempered ******* who everyone hates...

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: Gandall is right. Being around scoundrels for too long made me a scoundrel myself. No one respects me, nor do I deserve any respect.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You should talk to a therapist, family member, friend, or anyone who loves you... You need counseling and support.

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: Haha, well, I had someone like that. She was always by my side and gave me unconditional support. But I ruined everything with my own hands.

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: I yelled at her and neglected her. All I did when I got home was lose my temper. I broke the vows I gave at my wedding and made her life terrible. Even on the day she left, I couldn't muster up a decent apology.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: Then find her and apologize to her.

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: ...No need. She was right to leave. It's all for the best, both for her and me.
His gaze changes from despair to conviction, laced with a suffocating stubbornness.

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: People can't always make excuses for themselves. I screwed up, so I have to own up to it. I have to keep doing the only thing I'm good at: Being a good "inspector." Whenever I find a scumbag, I'll fight them to the end.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Pffft. Are you proud of that monologue?

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Ugh... Who's the one moaning on and on about his wife every time he drinks? So embarrassing. Aren't you too old to act like some lovesick teenager? I'm gonna retch. Blargh...

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: Ahem. Cough. Kids should shut up when the adults are talking... Wait, hold on, I've got a message.
Doyle's phone lights up. He checks it purposefully to change the subject, but the moment he sees the screen, he freezes and slams on the brakes. Everyone in the car yelps in shock.
When the car comes to a full stop, you see him staring at his phone in shock. After making a few calls, his hands tremble and his face turns ashen.

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: ...She was attacked by a Sleepwalker... She just got into the ICU. I can't get ahold of her, she...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: There are still many things you can do. Don't have any regrets.
Cursing violently, he grabs his gun out and stuffs it into your hand. Then he rams open the car door and rushes out. This is the first time you've seen him so passionate.

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: Then, you guys go first! Call me if anything happens! I promise I'll be back! Call me anytime!!

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Don't come back. We can handle it on our own...
Doyle flags down a taxi on the road and leaves. You wave at him as you connect to a call from the 9th Agency.

steps.speaker: Agent from the 9th Agency
steps.content: Are you happy with our arrangement, Chief ${PlayerName}?

steps.speaker: Choice
options: The inspector's wife isn't actually hurt, is she?

steps.speaker: Agent from the 9th Agency
steps.content: Of course not. We asked a hospital to cooperate with us, then temporarily jammed the inspector's wife's communications. Everything's played out like a soap opera.

steps.speaker: Agent from the 9th Agency
steps.content: Fortunately, Inspector Doyle got so worried that he didn't notice any flaws... He won't be able to return in a short time.
...But hope Doyle doesn't skin you alive when he finds out the truth.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: Thank you. In exchange, I have some special intel.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: In addition to the suppliers who have been rounded up, I also discovered Ambrosia at another place—the Midsummer Night's Club. An "entertainer" tried to trick me into drinking it.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: She was employed by Quinn as well. Their president also knew of my identity in advance. If you are interested, you can go check up on her details.

steps.speaker: Agent from the 9th Agency
steps.content: ...Haha, of course. We are always interested in intelligence about Quinn. It's a pleasure working with you.

steps.speaker: Agent from the 9th Agency
steps.content: Hope we are both successful in our endeavors.
You hang up. Speaking of which, that performer's "little trick" was quite interesting. You turn to the tied-up waiter, swishing the Ambrosia you got from Doyle.

steps.speaker: Bar Staff
steps.content: What... what are you going to do? I already brought you where you wanted to go! And I told you the place already!

steps.speaker: Bar Staff
steps.content: I'm just an ordinary guy! I have my life too, just like Doyle! I don't want to get involved with Sinners! You should let me go, too!

steps.speaker: Choice
options: But I still need some help from you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Selling Ambrosia can either be a serious or petty crime. I can say a few good words on your behalf...

steps.speaker: Bar Staff
steps.content: Huh...? Sob... are you the devil...
